messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'hotpath-us-east-1' exhausted. 429s spike across hotpath routes. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/xyz

eng_oncall_maya: Seeing queue growth on hotpath. avg queue length 1200 -> 5400 in 6m. 95th latency jumping, broad 429s. Paging SRE @sre_tom, infra @infra_ben

sre_tom: I'm on it. Can you dump autoscaler events + tokenbucket logs?

eng_oncall_maya: paste logs:
```
[autoscaler] scale_attempt pool=hotpath-us-east-1 requested=6->12 reason=queue_growth
[autoscaler] scale_rejected pool=hotpath-us-east-1 reason=max_pools_reached current=10 max=10
[ratelimit] token_refill tier=standard config_refill=50 unit=minute observed_refill=0.833 tokens/sec
[ratelimit] burst_size tier=standard=100
[proxy] 429 GET /v1/generate client=acme-app status=429 token_depleted
```

infra_ben: autoscaler hit customer quota limit (max_pools=10) from infra config change earlier today. ops changed quota to 10 for cost control.

pm_zoe: CS says multiple customers reporting errors, important ones hit: acme-app, shopline. Impact: degraded real-time features and timeouts.

sre_tom: Hmm ratelimit log shows `config_refill=50 unit=minute` – seems like unit mismatch. That would be ~0.83 r/s vs intended 50 r/s. Who pushed that change?

eng_oncall_maya: @infra_ben rolled out a ratepolicy.yaml change 02:17 with new units. Possibly accidentally used 'per_minute' semantics.

infra_ben: Confirmed. I pushed a rollback-ready change to staging but not prod. Rolling back now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout/ratepolicy-rollback id=rp-2026-03-15-02:44

eng_oncall_maya: Immediate mitigation: 1) bump token refill for standard tier to 500r/s 2) increase burst to 2000 3) temporarily raise pool max to 20 4) enable fallback to small-model for non-SLA traffic

sre_tom: Agreed. Commands:
```
infractl autoscale update --pool hotpath-us-east-1 --max 20
ratelimitctl set-tier --name standard --refill-rate 500 --burst 2000
infractl fallback enable --route /v1/generate --model small-economy --traffic 30%
```

infra_ben: Executed autoscale increase (accepted). Executed ratelimit patch. Fallback enabled at 30% for non-SLA keys.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: rollout/ratepolicy-rollback status=SUCCESS

eng_oncall_maya: Metrics: queue length dropping from 5400 -> 800 over 10m. 429 rate down from 18% -> 1.2%.

cs_miguel: Notifying top impacted customers now. Sending interim note: we hit capacity limits and applied mitigations; will follow up with timeline and RCA.

pm_zoe: Assigning postmortem owner. @sre_tom please lead, @infra_ben and @eng_oncall_maya as contributors. Timeline: Severity 2 (customer-impacting), begin RCA.

sre_tom: Accepted. Immediate action items for RCA:
- root cause: tokenbucket unit misconfig + autoscale quota too low
- why change passed: config review gap
- why autoscaler didn't pre-warn: monitoring thresholds too coarse

sre_tom: Overnight on-call handoff to @eng_oncall_maya -> @sre_tom for follow-ups. I'll capture runbook steps and add a guard.

eng_oncall_maya: Adding temporary alert rule: if queue > 1000 && scale_attempts_rejected > 0 alert paging to ops-leads and infra on-call.

infra_ben: Adding guardrail: block config deploys that change token units without explicit unit flag. Creating PR for validator.

pm_zoe: Customer escalation: cs_miguel to own comms, include ETA for permanent fix and timeline for quota increase request to infra finance.

cs_miguel: Sent initial outbound to 3 customers with incident token, awaiting replies. Will include workaround for graceful degrade.

sre_tom: Post-incident followups: 1) enforce config schema 2) increase default pool max for hotpath 3) add canary ratepolicy validation 4) playbook update for tokenbucket tuning. Assigning owners in doc.

eng_oncall_maya: Good job all. Marking this thread as incident in progress. Will update with final counts and postmortem link.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and tagged: incident_id=INC-2026-0543 severity=2 responders=[sre_tom,eng_oncall_maya,infra_ben]

cs_miguel: :thumbsup: Closing customer loop once RCA published.

sre_tom: Handover note for next shift: keep pool max=20 until postmortem complete, watch queue and 429s, escalate if >2% 429 sustained.

eng_oncall_maya: last check: 429s at 0.9% across hotpath, queue 350, autoscaler stable. Logging final metrics to incident doc.
